Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then use the required fish-control shelf and the visual-evidence skill before touching the candidate. I’ll trace the assigned parent, sampled outcomes, and inherited notes so the policy, candidate notes, and reusable guidance all point to the same evidence.

The visual-evidence skill applies because every sampled solver carries a combined wake sheet. I’m using it now to compare the best finite run with the most informative failures and to verify every visual impression against trajectory/force diagnostics before proposing an architecture. After that, the shelf’s invariant—not any published gain or route—will be translated into the two-joint feedback contract.

The comparison is already separating two failure classes. The inherited high-authority 2D-style controller self-propels well but clips almost continuously and cannot arrest post-pass yaw; the compact response-gated variants turn strongly yet initially move away, so “add more steering authority” is contradicted. I’m consulting the shelf now for a mechanism that preserves the traveling-wave carrier while making steering authority depend on observed turn response.

The evidence points to a mechanism change, not a gain sweep. Two compact mean-curvature loops independently drove the fish out through the upper boundary, while the assigned parent’s added yaw-arrest residual degraded the inherited approach and kept the clipping-dominated stack. I’m recording a falsifiable alternative before editing: an envelope-compatible traveling bend whose target command asymmetrically strengthens only the target-consistent posterior half-cycle, avoiding a persistent C-bend and beat-scale yaw-rate feedback.

The policy candidate is now one compact mechanism: the posterior lag is preserved, and target error only changes the relative strength of opposite half-cycles. The inherited lesson that recommended another yaw-response-to-curvature path is no longer supported by the completed parent and sibling results, so I’m revising it into a concrete negative boundary rather than preserving stale advice.

The guidance semantic check passes. The local Julia launcher is not on this shell’s `PATH`, so the first contract attempt did not execute; no candidate file was changed. I’m locating the workspace’s available Julia binary and will rerun the same non-CFD contract and dry joint-envelope checks explicitly.

The candidate passes the public policy call and a 60T joint-only envelope check. With mirrored target sides it produces mirrored posterior mean bends of about ±3.5°, while retaining roughly ±28° posterior motion; peak rates stay below 185°/T, peak accelerations below 1462°/T², and the 1700°/T² guard is never reached. This is only a contract/actuator check—not CFD evidence—and I’m recording that boundary explicitly in the notes.

All three local gates now pass: guidance change, Julia policy contract, and solver-boundary isolation. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check-runner for an independent non-CFD audit of the same candidate and will repair and rerun anything it flags.

The final diff is clean and scoped: one solver candidate, one provenance note, and one materially revised reusable lesson. The independent runner is still completing its Julia contract call; the already completed local checks found no schema, finiteness, guidance, or boundary violations.

Implemented exactly one Phase 2 candidate: bounded posterior half-cycle asymmetry around an envelope-compatible traveling-wave carrier.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:49)

Independent check-runner results: all PASS—guidance semantic change, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary isolation. The dry 60T joint check stayed below 185°/T and 1462°/T² without reaching the command guard. No CFD was run, as required.
